findings.title: Stop granting global group manage from the VIEW scope

response:
## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Security
Title: Stop granting global group manage from the VIEW scope

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:64-71

Explanation:
`canManage()` returns `true` when the all-groups permission grants either `VIEW` or `MANAGE`. A policy meant to grant read-only access to groups therefore also allows every operation guarded by `requireManage()`, such as creating top-level groups.

This is a privilege escalation. The Javadoc added in `GroupPermissionEvaluator` (lines 73-77) describes the same wrong behaviour, so it needs fixing too.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
@Override
public boolean canManage() {
    if (root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS)) {
        return true;
    }
    return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);
}
~~~

## 2) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Return group IDs and evaluate the correct resource in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:121-125

Explanation:
In `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup`, group resources are named by the group ID. Their resource `getId()` is an unrelated authz resource UUID. This method uses the resource ID in two places:

1. **The permission check is wrong.** `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` calls `resourceStore.findByName(server, <resource uuid>)`. That lookup never matches, so every group is evaluated against the all-groups resource instead of its own per-group permissions.
2. **The returned IDs are wrong.** `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` returns resource UUIDs, not group IDs.

`UsersResource` and `BruteForceUsersResource` place this set in `UserModel.GROUPS` and pass it to `getUsersCount(...)`, where group IDs are expected. As a result, user search and count filtering by group membership is wrong: users may be missing, or counts may be wrong.

Also, `findByType` may return the type-level "Groups" resource itself. That resource is not a group ID and should be skipped.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, groupResource -> {
    if (AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE.equals(groupResource.getName())) return; // skip type resource
    String groupId = groupResource.getName();
    if (hasPermission(groupId, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW_MEMBERS, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE_MEMBERS)) {
        granted.add(groupId);
    }
});
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Security
Title: Confirm per-user view filtering still runs on user search results

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/UsersResource.java:448-453

Explanation:
The old code filtered results with `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` before building representations. That filter is now removed.

Group filtering via `UserModel.GROUPS` is only applied when `groupIds` is non-empty. If the caller has `query-users` but no view permission and no group grants, `searchForUserStream` returns all users unfiltered. Unless `toRepresentation` (not shown in this diff) applies `canView`, those users would be exposed.

The new test (`testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers`) expects an empty result, which suggests filtering happens somewhere. However, this cannot be verified from the diff, and the removal also drops a defence-in-depth check.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
return toRepresentation(realm, usersEvaluator, briefRepresentation,
        session.users().searchForUserStream(realm, attributes, firstResult, maxResults).filter(usersEvaluator::canView));
~~~
Alternatively, verify that `toRepresentation` filters by `canView` and document that.

## 4) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Prevent group deletion from failing with UnsupportedOperationException in V2 realms

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:172-175
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:74-98

Explanation:
The provider event listener handles `GroupRemovedEvent` by calling `management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false)`. Now that `MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()` returns `GroupPermissionsV2`, that call throws `UnsupportedOperationException`.

If `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` (V1) is enabled at the same time as a realm that uses V2 permissions, deleting a group would fail. This depends on how `management()` picks V2, which is outside the diff.

Either make the V2 method a no-op (or clean up the V2 group resource), or skip the V1 cleanup for V2 realms.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
@Override
public void setPermissionsEnabled(GroupModel group, boolean enable) {
    if (enable) throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2");
    // no-op on removal; optionally delete V2 resource for the group
}
~~~

## 5) Severity: LOW | Type: Doc
Title: Fix incorrect Javadoc references in GroupPermissionEvaluator

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:132-135
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:142-147

Explanation:
- The `requireManageMembers` Javadoc says it throws based on `canManageMembership`; it should reference `canManageMembers`.
- `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` documents a return of "Stream of IDs", but it returns a `Set`.

Misleading docs on authorization APIs make security reviews harder.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
/** Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembers(GroupModel)} returns {@code false}. */
void requireManageMembers(GroupModel group);
...
/** @return Set of IDs of groups whose members the caller can view. */
~~~

true_positives.golden_comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

Both comments point to the same privilege escalation bug in the permission fallback logic.

This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

The golden comment explains this in more detail, noting the mismatch between what hasPermission expects (group id/resource name) versus what it receives (resource UUID), and how this affects the filtering and counts. Both identify the same fundamental bug - using the wrong identifier type in the permission check.
